options: The internal name for Salesforce's own Sales Cloud product
Salesforce's marketplace where companies and developers distribute applications and components built on the platform
A tool exclusively for writing code in Developer Console
A support ticketing system for Salesforce customers
questions.explain: AppExchange, launched in 2005, is where applications and components built on the Salesforce Platform get packaged and made available to other customers.

questions.q: Besides full applications, what else does this lesson say is listed on AppExchange?
options: Only free trial licenses for Salesforce itself
Only mobile phone hardware
Nothing else — it lists full applications exclusively
Components, Lightning data sets, and consultants available to hire
questions.explain: The lesson lists components that extend a screen, ready-to-use external data sets, and consultants as additional listing types.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should someone check before installing an AppExchange app into a production org?
options: Only whether the listing's icon looks professional
Nothing — all listings are pre-vetted and safe by default
What it costs, what data access it requires, and what other customers say in the reviews
Only the publisher's phone number
questions.explain: The lesson recommends reading the listing closely — pricing, data access, and reviews — before installing anything into a real org.

questions.q: What does "ISV" stand for, as used in this lesson?
options: Internal Salesforce Verification
Installed Service Version
Integrated Sales Visibility
Independent Software Vendor
questions.explain: An ISV is a company that builds and sells software on the Salesforce Platform, part of the partner ecosystem.

questions.q: What does this lesson say the partner ecosystem explains about Salesforce careers?
options: That only Salesforce itself ever hires Salesforce consultants
It's a major reason Salesforce careers exist outside companies that simply use Salesforce internally — partner firms hire consultants and developers to build solutions for other companies
That the partner ecosystem has no connection to career opportunities at all
That consultants can only be hired directly by Salesforce, never through AppExchange
questions.explain: Partner firms — consulting companies and ISVs — hire people whose entire job is building and implementing Salesforce solutions for other businesses.
